groups.title: Cough and Phlegm Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for cough and phlegm.
groups.usage: For adults, 2 capsules per dose, 3 times a day after meals.
groups.caution: This medicine must not be taken by people who are hypersensitive to it, by women who are or may be pregnant, by infants under 3 months of age, by people who are taking an MAO inhibitor (such as an antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser or anti-Parkinson medicine) or who stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks, or by people with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Cough and phlegm
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Pregnancy; infants under 3 months; MAO inhibitors

groups.title: Anti-inflammatory Analgesic Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), ankylosing spondylitis, tendinitis, acute gout, dysmenorrhoea and bursitis, and for skeletal muscle disorders (sprain, bruise, injury), lumbosacral pain, pain after surgery, migraine and pain after a tooth extraction.
groups.usage: For adults, for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis and ankylosing spondylitis, 1 to 2 capsules (250 to 500 mg) per dose, 2 times a day (every 12 hours). For acute gout, take 3 capsules (750 mg) as the first dose, then 1 capsule (250 mg) at intervals of 8 hours until the attack has gone. For skeletal muscle disorders, pain after surgery, pain after a tooth extraction, dysmenorrhoea, tendinitis and bursitis, take 2 capsules (500 mg) as the first dose, then 1 capsule (250 mg) at intervals of 6 to 8 hours. See the approved product information for the remaining dosing details.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause gastrointestinal bleeding. This medicine may increase the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, which can be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal reactions such as bleeding, ulcer and perforation may occur. It must not be taken by people who are hypersensitive to this medicine or to aspirin. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, acute gout, period pain, pain after surgery
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Aspirin allergy; regular alcohol use; heart or stomach problems

groups.usage: For adults, 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 4 times a day. Do not exceed 4 capsules (1200 mg) a day.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause gastrointestinal bleeding. summaryTable.Use: Arthritis and joint inflammation; pain and swelling after injury or surgery

groups.title: Children's Anti-inflammatory Analgesic Syrup
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain due to a cold, low back pain, dysmenorrhoea, pain after surgery, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprain, bruise) and non-articular rheumatic disease.
groups.usage: For children aged 11 to 14 years, 200 to 250 mg (10 to 13 mL) per dose; for children aged 7 to 10 years, 150 to 200 mg (8 to 10 mL) per dose; for children aged 3 to 6 years, 100 to 150 mg (5 to 8 mL) per dose; and for children aged 1 to 2 years, 50 to 100 mg (3 to 5 mL) per dose, taken 3 to 4 times a day. For children weighing less than 30 kg, the daily amount must not exceed 500 mg (25 mL), and it is best to avoid giving it on an empty stomach.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause gastrointestinal bleeding. This medicine may increase the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, which can be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal reactions such as bleeding, ulcer and perforation may occur. People with uncontrolled high blood pressure should take particular care. Before giving it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Arthritis; fever and pain from a cold; headache, toothache, muscle and joint pain
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Dosing by age and weight; stomach, heart or blood pressure problems

groups.title: Cold Relief Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 1 tablet per dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause liver damage. Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Cold symptoms: sore throat, cough, phlegm, fever, headache, aches
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 15 years; regular alcohol use; skin rash after taking

groups.title: Nasal Symptom Relief Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing, watery eyes, sore throat and a heavy feeling in the head caused by a nasal cold (acute rhinitis), allergic rhinitis or sinusitis.
groups.usage: For people aged 15 years and over and adults, 1 capsule per dose, 3 times a day after meals. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution: If a serious skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist. It must not be taken by people who are hypersensitive to it, by children under 2 years of age, by children under 15 years of age, by people who are taking an MAO inhibitor (such as an antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser or anti-Parkinson medicine) or who stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks, or by people with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure. summaryTable.Use: Nasal congestion, runny nose, sneezing and watery eyes from a cold or rhinitis

groups.title: Children's Fever Reducer Syrup
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to reduce fever caused by an acute upper respiratory tract infection.
groups.usage: For children aged 6 months and over, 0.4 to 0.6 mL/kg per dose (5 to 7 mg/kg), taken as needed at intervals of 4 to 6 hours, up to a maximum of 4 doses a day (28 mg/kg). For children weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed a maximum of 25 mL (300 mg) a day. If the child's weight is known, dosing by weight is more appropriate, so see the approved product information for the recommended dose by age group.
groups.caution: Anyone who regularly drinks 3 or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic, as it may cause gastrointestinal bleeding. This medicine may increase the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, which can be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal reactions such as bleeding, ulcer and perforation may occur. summaryTable.Use: Fever due to an acute upper respiratory tract infection (children)
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 6 months; dosing by body weight; stomach or heart problems

groups.title: Enteric-coated Laxative Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve constipation and the poor appetite, abdominal bloating, abnormal fermentation in the bowel and haemorrhoids that come with constipation.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 3 times a day after meals, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours between doses. Take the smallest amount for the first dose, then increase or decrease it a little at a time while watching the form and condition of the stools.
groups.caution: This medicine must not be taken by people with an acute abdominal disease (such as appendicitis, intestinal bleeding or ulcerative colitis), intestinal obstruction or hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption, or by children aged 10 years and under. Before taking it, people with severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting, women who are or may be pregnant, and people on a sodium-restricted diet should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Constipation and the poor appetite, bloating and haemorrhoids that come with it
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Age 10 years and under; severe abdominal pain; pregnancy

groups.title: Antihistamine Tablet for Allergy
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria, itchy skin, eczema and dermatitis (used together with a hydrocortisone product applied to the skin).
groups.usage: For adults and children aged 6 years and over, 10 mg once a day by mouth before bedtime. For patients who are sensitive to side effects, 5 mg in divided doses in the morning and evening. The dose may be increased or decreased as appropriate for age and symptoms. For patients with kidney impairment, see the approved product information for the dosing interval.
groups.caution: This medicine must not be taken by people who are hypersensitive to it, by people with kidney failure, by infants under 6 years of age, or by people with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking it, pregnant women, breastfeeding women, older people, people with kidney or liver impairment, people with epilepsy or a risk of seizures, and people with a condition that predisposes them to urine retention (such as a spinal cord lesion or prostate problems) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Allergic rhinitis and conjunctivitis, chronic urticaria, itchy skin, dermatitis
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Under 6 years; kidney or liver problems; epilepsy; urine retention

groups.title: Vitamin D and B Complex Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to supply vitamins D, B1, B2 and B6 in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breastfeeding, when strength is low during or after illness, during growth periods and in old age, to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain and joint pain (such as low back pain and stiff shoulders), and for beriberi and eye strain.
groups.usage: For adults aged 19 years and over, 1 tablet per dose, once a day after a meal.
groups.caution: This medicine must not be taken by people who are hypersensitive to it, by people with hypercalcaemia (too much calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease, kidney stones or hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption, or by infants under 3 months of age. Before taking it, infants under 1 year of age and other people at risk should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Vitamin D, B1, B2 and B6 supply; neuralgia, muscle and joint pain; eye strain
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Infants under 3 months; high blood calcium; kidney disease or stones

groups.title: Oral Contraceptive Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for contraception and for the treatment of moderate acne in women who are able to take this medicine.
groups.usage: Take 1 tablet a day for 21 days, at the same time each day, then have a 7-day break. See the approved product information for details.
groups.caution: Women taking oral contraceptives should avoid smoking, because the risk of serious cardiovascular events such as thrombosis may increase. Smokers aged 35 years and over must not take this medicine. It must also not be taken by people who are hypersensitive to it, people with an oestrogen-dependent tumour (for example endometrial cancer), people who have or are suspected of having breast cancer or who have had it, people who have or have had thrombophlebitis or thromboembolism, people with deep vein thrombosis, or people with an inherited or acquired tendency to thrombosis. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Contraception; treatment of moderate acne in eligible women
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Smoking, age 35 years and over; blood clots; breast cancer

groups.caution: This medicine must not be taken by children under 15 years of age or by people with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking it, people who have had allergic symptoms from a medicine or cosmetic product (rash, redness, itching), people who have had allergic symptoms to egg (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching), and people with an allergic constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Supportive treatment for gingivitis and mild to moderate periodontitis

groups.title: Anti-inflammatory Analgesic Soft Capsule
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used for fever and pain due to a cold, low back pain, period pain, rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), pain after surgery, headache, migraine, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, ankylosing spondylitis, acute gout and psoriasis-related joint disease.
groups.usage: For adults, for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, 1 to 3 capsules (200 to 600 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times a day, up to a maximum of 16 capsules (3200 mg) a day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight a day in 3 to 4 divided doses. For mild to moderate pain or a cold, adults take 1 to 2 capsules (200 to 400 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times a day. For migraine, adults take 1 to 2 capsules per dose. See the approved product information for the remaining dosing details.
groups.caution: This medicine must not be taken by people who are hypersensitive to it, or who have a gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe heart failure, severe high blood pressure or bronchial asthma; people who have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction caused by aspirin or another anti-inflammatory painkiller; people with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; women in the last 3 months of pregnancy; breastfeeding women; or people receiving high-dose methotrexate as cancer treatment. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Arthritis, gout; fever and pain from a cold; headache, toothache, muscle pain
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Aspirin or NSAID allergy; stomach ulcer; heart, liver or kidney disease; pregnancy

groups.title: Anti-inflammatory Analgesic Tablet
groups.efficacy: This medicine is used to relieve mild to moderate pain such as muscle pain, neuralgia, pain after injury or surgery, headache, toothache and earache.
groups.usage: For adults, 1 to 2 tablets (125 to 250 mg) per dose, 3 times a day.
groups.caution: This medicine must not be taken by people with peptic ulcer; people in whom a medicine has caused stomach or duodenal upset; people who are hypersensitive to this medicine; people who have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory painkiller (including COX-2 inhibitors); people being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery; women who are or may be pregnant; or people with severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe heart failure or Crohn's disease. Before taking it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.Use: Mild to moderate pain: muscle pain, neuralgia, headache, toothache, earache
summaryTable.Check with a pharmacist: Aspirin or NSAID allergy; peptic ulcer; heart, liver or kidney disease; pregnancy
